findings.title: Generation observation can become stale before the seal commits
findings.detail: PARTIALLY_FIXED by static inspection. The handler now observes provider generations before runSourceCommand, correctly rejecting an already replaced or missing object. However, it subsequently acquires the revision lock at line 76 and compares files only with the cached observation at lines 115–120. No provider protection binds that observation through the seal commit. A provider replacement while the command waits therefore leaves persisted admission and evaluation unchanged and still allows sealing the unavailable generation. The comment at line 30 explicitly delegates replacements after observation to inventory reconciliation, preserving this portion of the original gap against CMD017-DENY. The passing regression at apps/api/test/cmd017-seal-revision.test.ts:245 replaces the object before stat returns; it does not cover the reverse ordering.
findings.reproduction: Using readyRevision and acceptedOf from apps/api/test/cmd017-seal-revision.test.ts, hold the revision row in an otherwise unchanged transaction. Start SealRevision and wait for its API revision-lock wait, so its provider stat has already returned the accepted generation. Overwrite that accepted object using plantObject(..., { overwrite: true }), then release the revision lock without changing revision or admission facts. The handler consumes the cached observation and reaches the normal seal commit without another provider check. This interleaving was established by code inspection, not executed in the read-only review.

findings.title: Per-association counts are preserved through evaluation and sealing
findings.detail: FIXED. tablesWithAssociations validates and attaches the evaluator's association counts to their declared tables; line 120 persists those tables and line 144 includes them in the evaluation hash. SealRevision reads the typed counts and checks uniqueness, completeness and their sum at packages/application/src/sources/handlers/seal-revision.ts:368. The integrated regression at apps/control/test/end-to-end.test.ts:199 exercises SelectInputTables, the real consumer and SealRevision; assertions at lines 260–264 compare persisted and sealed counts with independently calculated totals. verify.log:638 records its pass.
findings.reproduction: The historical two-association path is now covered end to end: it returns SEALED and preserves the distinct WORKS_AT and OWNED_BY counts instead of raising INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

findings.title: Excluded hidden columns no longer feed projection counts
findings.detail: FIXED. Insertion into byColumn now requires the same counted predicate that governs formula validation. Lines 215–217 also reject projection keys or fields referencing excluded hidden columns with PROJECTION_COLUMN_HIDDEN. The regression at packages/data-plane/test/selection-evaluation.test.ts:371 covers the original hidden formula, hidden field references, included-column formula rejection, cached-value counting and a visible-column positive control. verify.log:614 records its pass.
findings.reproduction: The original hidden-B projection under EXCLUDE and REJECT_FORMULAS now fails PROJECTION_COLUMN_HIDDEN. Including B applies the formula policy; projecting only the visible column still succeeds.

findings.title: Lapsed unresolved cancellation secrets are discovered and purged
findings.detail: FIXED. Reconciliation separately pages agencies with lapsed pending cancellations and discovers their remaining secret rows under agency scope. The queries at packages/persistence/src/source/uploads.ts:388 and :404 include expired horizons. The sweep invokes cancelProviderSession at line 66, whose horizon branch at apps/control/src/storage-work.ts:140 purges the secret without inventing cancellation confirmation. The regression at apps/control/test/storage-lifecycle.test.ts:295 checks UNCERTAIN before and after expiry, secret removal, no additional provider call and pagination past previously cleaned agencies. verify.log:657 records its pass.
findings.reproduction: The historical sequence now retains the secret while reconciliation remains uncertain before expiry, then removes it on a post-horizon sweep while preserving UNCERTAIN. A later agency remains discoverable with a sweep limit of one.
